content.text: Education AI is a comprehensive School Management System that covers every aspect of school administration - from student enrollment and attendance tracking to finance, HR, academics, examinations, transport, library, and more. The system supports multiple user roles and provides dedicated portals for administrators, teachers, parents, and students.
The system supports the following roles, each with different access levels:

rows: Full access; can create users within their school
School operations; can create staff-level users
Academics, content creation, classes and students

content.text: User Management: School Admins can create Principal, Manager, Accountant, Teacher, Staff and Driver users. Principals can create Manager, Accountant, Teacher, Staff and Driver users. See the User Management chapter for full details.
Open the application URL in your web browser.
Enter your username/email and password on the Login page.
Click 'Sign In' to access your dashboard.
If you manage multiple schools, use the School Switcher (top bar) to select the active school.

content.title: First-Time Setup
content.text: Your School Admin account is pre-configured for you. Once you receive your credentials, log in and follow the Initial Setup steps in Chapter 2. You can then create other users from Settings > Users tab.

The application uses a sidebar on the left side of the screen. Groups expand to show their pages. What you see depends on your role and on which modules your school has enabled. On mobile devices, the sidebar collapses into a menu button.
School name and School Switcher - Switch between schools if you have access to several schools
Academic Year switcher - Change the active academic year/session
Light/Dark mode toggle
Notification Bell - View unread notifications
Your name and user menu - Profile settings, logout
Dashboard - Main overview page
Attendance - 1. Manual Entry, 2. Face Attendance, Attendance Record
Finance - Dashboard, Accounts, Fee Overview, Collect Payments, Fee Setup, Other Income, Expenses, Discounts
Academics - Subjects, Timetable, then under Assessment: Exam Types, Exams, Assessments, Marks Entry, Grade Scale, Results, Report Cards, Assignments
Content Creation - Question Bank, Paper Builder, Question Papers, Worksheets, Curriculum
Planning & Delivery - Curriculum Coverage, Lesson Plans
AI Analytics and Academic Risk
HR & Staff - Dashboard, Staff Directory, Departments, Salary, Payroll, Leave, Attendance, Performance, Documents, Letter Composer, Staff Risk
Management - Classes, Students, Student Risk Score, Recently Deleted, Academic Calendar, Sessions, Promotion
Notifications and Messages
Admissions - Enquiries, Conversion Likelihood
Transport, Library, Hostel, Inventory
User Guide, School Setup, Settings

Teachers see a shorter menu: Dashboard, Attendance for their own classes, Academics (Timetable, Exam Schedule, Assessments, Marks Entry, Results, Report Cards, Assignments), Content Creation, Planning & Delivery, My Leave, My Attendance, Notifications and Messages.
Dashboard, Leave Requests, Messages and User Guide.
Dashboard, Attendance, Fees, Timetable, Exam Schedule, Results, Assignments, Library, Transport, AI Study Helper, My Profile and User Guide.

content.title: Missing a menu item?
content.text: If you cannot see a page, your role may not have access to it, or the module is not enabled for your school. Ask your School Admin.
Before using the system, you must set up foundational data in the correct order. Each step depends on the previous one being completed. Follow this sequence carefully.

The setup order matters! For example, you cannot add students before creating classes, and you cannot create exams before setting up academic years and subjects. Follow the order below to avoid errors.
Log in with your School Admin credentials.
Navigate to Management > Sessions in the sidebar.
In the 'Years' tab, click 'Add Academic Year'.
Enter: Name (e.g., '2025-2026'), Start Date, End Date.
Click 'Set as Current' to make it the active year.
Switch to the 'Terms' tab and click 'Add Term'.
Enter: Name (e.g., 'Term 1'), Term Type (Term/Semester/Quarter), Start Date, End Date, Order.
Add all terms for the academic year.

content.title: Why This Matters
content.text: Academic years and terms are required for exams, report cards, fee structures, and student promotions. Set this up first.
Navigate to 'Classes' in the sidebar under Management.
Keep master classes simple: create one section-free class per grade, such as Playgroup, Nursery, Prep, Class 1, and Class 2.
Click 'Add Class', choose the Grade Level, confirm the Class Name, and save without adding sections.
Repeat once per grade level. The master class list is the shared class catalog used across academic years.
After master classes are ready, switch to Session Classes for the active academic year and create sections such as A, B, and C there.
Classes are displayed grouped by grade level. Use the 'Grid' toggle for an alternate view.

content.title: Tip
content.text: Create sections in Session Classes, not in the master catalog. Example: keep master 'Class 5' once, then create session sections 'Class 5 - A' and 'Class 5 - B' inside the selected academic year.
Navigate to 'Students' in the sidebar under Management.
To add one student: Click 'Add Student' and fill in Name, Roll Number, Class, Parent Name, Parent Phone, Admission Number.
To bulk import: Click 'Import from Excel', download the template, fill it in, and upload.
Students will appear in the list. Use the class filter to view students by class.
You can export the student list as PDF, PNG, or Excel using the export buttons.
Students must be assigned to a class. Make sure classes are created (Step 2) before adding students.

content.title: Session Enrollment
content.text: When you add a student (individually or via Excel upload), the system automatically creates an enrollment record for the school's current academic year. This links the student to the correct session. Roll numbers are unique per session and class, so different academic years can have different students with the same roll number in the same class.
Navigate to Academics > Subjects in the sidebar.
In the 'Subjects' tab, click 'Add Subject'.
Enter: Subject Name, Subject Code, Description, and whether it is an Elective.
Save. Repeat for all subjects taught in the school.
Switch to the 'Assignments' tab to assign subjects to classes.
Select a class, pick a subject, choose the teacher, set periods per week, then save.
Navigate to Academics > Timetable.
Select a class to create its timetable.
Define time slots (period start time, end time).
Assign subjects and teachers to each period for each day of the week.
Save the timetable. Students and parents can now view it in their portals.

content.title: Prerequisite
content.text: Subjects must be assigned to classes (Step 4) before creating timetables.
Use this table to understand what must be set up before each feature works:

School Admins and Principals can use the School Setup wizard instead of visiting each page. It walks through the setup in order: School Profile, Academic Year, Session Classes, Classes & Grades, Students, Staff & HR, Subjects, Finance, and Review & Finish. Steps for modules your school does not use are skipped.
Open 'School Setup' in the sidebar.
Complete each step, then press 'Next Step'. Press 'Skip' to leave a step for later.
Press 'Exit Setup' at any time to leave; you can return later.
On the last step, review your setup and press 'Go to Dashboard'.

content.title: When to use it
content.text: Use the wizard for a new school. For later changes, use the individual pages described in Steps 1-5 above.
Teachers and admins mark daily attendance class by class with Manual Entry, or by camera with Face Attendance (Chapter 4). The Attendance Record page shows the monthly register.

content.title: Teacher Access
content.text: Teachers see only the classes assigned to them by the school. Admins and Principals see all classes.
Open 'Attendance' in the sidebar and choose '1. Manual Entry'.
Pick the Class (sections appear as 'Class 1 - A' for the active academic year).
The Date is today by default. Change it if you are marking a past day.
The student list appears with roll number, name and a status button. At first every status shows 'Not Set'.
To start quickly, press 'Mark All Present'. You can also use 'Mark All Absent', 'Mark All Leave' or 'Reset All'.
Tap a student's status to change it. Each tap cycles Not Set, Present, Absent, Leave.
The counts above the list (Present, Absent, Leave, Total) update as you go.
Press 'Save Attendance'. The button shows how many students will be saved.
A green message confirms the result, for example 'Saved! 4 created, 0 updated.'
On OFF days (days the school marked as non-working, such as holidays) attendance is not applicable and the Save button is disabled.

sections.title: Correcting Attendance That Is Already Marked

content.text: Open Manual Entry and choose the same Class and Date.
A blue notice says 'Attendance records already exist for this date. Saving will update them.' The saved statuses are loaded.
Tap a student's status to correct it.
Press 'Save Attendance'. The message shows records updated, for example 'Saved! 0 created, 4 updated.' Nothing is duplicated.
Choose 'Attendance Record' under Attendance.
Select a Class.
Use the month arrows to move between months.
The register is a grid: students in rows, days of the month in columns, with each student's mark in the cell.
Students who joined or left mid-month, and approved away periods, are shown differently from normal absences.
Use the download button to save the register as a PDF.

rows: No mark yet; it is not saved

content.text: The Face Attendance module uses AI-powered face recognition to take attendance from a single group photo of the class. Instead of marking each student by hand, a teacher or admin takes a photo of the class, and the system automatically detects faces, matches them to enrolled students, and marks attendance. This is faster and works well for classes where camera-based attendance is preferred.

content.title: How It Works
content.text: 1. Enroll each student by uploading a clear portrait photo (one-time setup). 2. Take a group photo of the class. 3. The AI detects all faces, matches them to enrolled students, and flags uncertain matches. 4. Review the results and confirm attendance.
Face Enrollment is required before using face attendance. Students without an enrolled face photo cannot be matched automatically. Enroll all students in a class before capturing attendance.
Before using Face Attendance, ensure:
Classes are created with students enrolled (see Chapter 2)
The face recognition library is installed on the server (dlib + face_recognition)
Supabase storage bucket is configured for image uploads

content.path: Sidebar > Attendance > 2. Face Attendance > Manage Enrollments

content.text: Enrollment is a one-time setup where you upload a clear portrait photo of each student. The system extracts a facial fingerprint (embedding) that is used for matching during attendance.
Navigate to Face Attendance and click 'Manage Enrollments' (top-right button).
Select a Class from the dropdown on the left panel.
Select a Student from the student dropdown (shows all students in the class).
Upload or capture a clear portrait photo of the student. The photo must show exactly one face.
Click 'Enroll Face'. The system uploads the photo, detects the face, and stores the facial embedding.
The enrolled student appears in the right panel with a quality score percentage.
Repeat for all students in the class.

content.title: Photo Tips
content.text: Use a clear, well-lit portrait photo with the student facing the camera. Avoid group photos, sunglasses, or heavy shadows. Quality score above 70% is recommended. The right panel shows all enrolled students with quality scores. To remove an enrollment, click 'Remove' next to the student and confirm.

content.path: Sidebar > Attendance > 2. Face Attendance > Group Photo Tab

content.text: Once students are enrolled, you can take attendance by capturing a group photo of the class.
Navigate to Face Attendance. You will see the Group Photo tab (default).
The page also has a Mobile Capture tab (live camera capture) and a Sessions tab (past sessions).
Select the Class from the dropdown.
Select the Date (defaults to today).
Click 'Select or Capture Photo' to take a photo using the device camera or upload an existing image.
A preview of the photo appears. Click 'Clear' to retake if needed.
Click 'Process Attendance'. The photo is uploaded and the AI begins processing.
You are automatically navigated to the Review page.

content.path: Sidebar > Attendance > 2. Face Attendance > Review Page

content.text: After processing (10-30 seconds), the Review page shows three sections: the captured photo, a grid of detected face thumbnails with match info, and the Class Roll with present/absent toggles. The page auto-refreshes while processing.
Review the detected faces grid. Remove incorrect detections with the red X button.
In the Class Roll, click any student to toggle Present/Absent. AI-matched students are auto-marked Present; unmatched are marked Absent.
After reviewing and adjusting the present/absent selections, click 'Confirm Attendance'.
The system saves attendance records for all students in the class (Present or Absent).
A success message appears and the session status changes to 'Confirmed' (green badge).
Confirmed attendance records appear in the Attendance Record register alongside manually entered records.

content.title: Reprocessing
content.text: If you are unsatisfied with the AI results, click 'Reprocess' to re-run face detection and matching on the same photo. This clears existing detections and starts fresh.

content.path: Sidebar > Attendance > 2. Face Attendance > Sessions Tab

content.text: Click the 'Sessions' tab on the Face Attendance page.
View all past sessions with class name, date, face count, and status badge.
Click any session to open the Review page (view confirmed results or review pending ones).
Session statuses: Processing (blue), Needs Review (yellow), Confirmed (green), Failed (red).
The AI uses distance-based matching to compare detected faces against enrolled student photos. Matches are classified into three categories based on confidence:
Click 'Add Subject' to create a new subject.
Fill in: Subject Name, Code (e.g., MATH, ENG), Description.
Check 'Is Elective' if the subject is optional for students.
Save. The subject appears in the list with AI-generated insights about workload.
Switch to the 'Assignments' tab.
Click 'Assign Subject' and select: Class, Subject, Teacher, Periods Per Week.
Save. This links the subject, teacher, and class together.
Repeat for all subject-class-teacher combinations.

Academic sessions define the school calendar and are critical for exams, promotions, and reports. All student data - attendance, fees, exams, roll numbers - is scoped to the active academic session. Use the Academic Year Switcher in the header to view data for any session.
In the 'Years' tab, view all academic years.
Click 'Add Academic Year' to create a new one (Name, Start Date, End Date).
Click 'Set as Current' on the year you want to make active.
The year summary shows: number of terms, exams created, students enrolled.

content.title: Session-Scoped Data
content.text: When you switch the academic year in the header, all pages update to show data for that session: Students, Attendance, Fees, Exams, and more. Roll numbers are assigned per session, so the same class can have different students with roll number 1 in different academic years.
Switch to the 'Terms' tab.
Filter by Academic Year if needed.
Click 'Add Term' and fill in: Name, Type (Term/Semester/Quarter), Order, Dates.
Terms define when exams happen and how report cards are structured.
In the 'Terms' tab, click 'Import Terms'.
Select Source Academic Year and Target Academic Year, then choose Conflict Mode: Skip Existing or Update Existing.
Click 'Preview Import' to review what will be created, updated, or skipped with adjusted dates.
Click 'Import Terms' to apply the import. Use this at the start of a new session to save setup time and keep term structure consistent.
Select the source academic year and source class/session class.
Select the target academic year.
Review each student row and choose an action: PROMOTE, REPEAT, or GRADUATE.
For PROMOTE/REPEAT, confirm the target class or target session class and set roll numbers as needed.
Use preview helpers where available, then run bulk promotion.
After execution, open the Promotion History tab to verify generated event rows.
PROMOTE: Student moves to next class in the target academic year; source enrollment becomes PROMOTED.
REPEAT: Student remains at same grade intent in the target academic year; source enrollment becomes REPEAT.
GRADUATE: Student is marked terminal graduate in source context; no target class is required.
If a promotion result is wrong, use Correct Single or Correct Bulk from Promotion History.
Provide source/target years and the correction action.
For REPEAT corrections, the system now normalizes stale promoted targets to same-grade repeat targets automatically.
When session-class IDs differ across years, correction resolves target-year session class mapping safely.
Promotion and correction are audited operations. Always verify source year, target year, and class mappings before confirming.

content.title: Promotion & New Admissions
content.text: New admissions can happen in a future session before promotion is run for the current session. For example, you can admit students to Playgroup for 2026-27 while 2025-26 students are still in Playgroup. Roll numbers are independent per session, so there are no conflicts. When you promote the old students, they move to the next class.

The AI Analytics page provides intelligent insights about academic performance, subject workload balance, attendance correlation with grades, and more. Use it to identify struggling students and subjects that need attention.
The Academic Calendar is a large month view of sessions, terms, off-days and school events.
Choose the Academic Year, and filter by Class or 'Whole School'.
Use the Year and Month selectors and the Previous/Next buttons to move around.
Press 'Add Event / Off Day' to add an entry.
Enter the Title and Type, and switch on 'OFF Day' if school is closed.
Choose who it applies to (Students, Staff or both) and the scope (whole school or specific classes).
For off-days, pick an OFF Day Category (for example Summer Vacation or Religious Holiday).
Set the Start and End Date, an optional Color Tag and Description, then save.
Sundays are marked OFF automatically.
The side panel lists Terms touching the month, Entries in the month and Exam groups this month.
Calendar Completeness shows how many days of the month are configured.
Attendance cannot be saved on OFF days (see Chapter 3).
The Examinations module covers the complete exam lifecycle: defining grade scales, creating exam types, scheduling exams, entering marks, viewing results, and generating report cards.
Navigate to Academics > Grade Scale in the sidebar.
Click 'Add Grade' and define each grade level.
For each grade, enter: Grade Name (A+, A, B+...), Min Marks, Max Marks, Grade Point (GPA).
Save all grades. This scale is used to auto-calculate student grades from marks.
Click 'Add Exam Type'.
Enter: Type Name (e.g., 'Mid-Term Exam', 'Final Exam', 'Unit Test').
Set the weightage (how much this exam type counts toward the final grade).
Save. Exam types can be reused across terms and years.
Click 'Create Exam'.
Select: Academic Year, Term, Class, Exam Type.
Enter: Exam Name, Start Date, End Date.
The exam status will be 'SCHEDULED' initially.
As the exam progresses, update status: SCHEDULED > IN_PROGRESS > MARKS_ENTRY > COMPLETED > PUBLISHED.
Select the Exam, Class, and Subject from the dropdowns.
The system loads all students in that class.
Enter marks for each student. The max marks are validated automatically.
Save marks. You can return and edit marks until the exam is published.
Bulk import from Excel is also available for large classes.
Select the Exam and Class to view computed results.
Results show: Subject-wise marks, grades (auto-calculated from grade scale), GPA.
Review results for accuracy.
Click 'Generate AI Comments' to create personalized per-subject comments for all students.
Click on any student row to expand and view/edit their AI-generated comments.

To make results visible to students and parents, open Sidebar > Academics > Exams, find the exam group and click 'Announce Results' (or 'Announce Ready Classes' if some classes are still missing marks). The button stays disabled until all marks for that exam are entered.
Select a Class from the dropdown to filter students.
Search or select the student from the filtered list (sorted by roll number).
Optionally filter by Academic Year and Term.
Preview the report card with all exam results, grades, and GPA.
Click 'Download PDF' to generate a printable report card with the school logo, marks table, grade scale reference, and page footer.

content.path: Sidebar > Settings > School Profile > Examination Settings

content.text: Schools can choose between two calculation modes for report cards:
Simple Average (default) - All exam marks summed and divided by total possible marks.
Weighted Average - Each exam type contributes based on its weight (e.g., Mid-Term 30%, Final 70%). Enable this toggle if your institution uses weighted grading.
Go to Settings > School Profile and scroll to 'Examination Settings'.
Toggle 'Weighted Average' ON or OFF.
When enabled, set appropriate weights on each Exam Type (Step 2 above).

content.title: Complete Exam Workflow
content.text: Grade Scale > Exam Types > Create Exam > Enter Marks > View Results > Publish > Report Cards. Each step depends on the previous one.

Separately from exam marks, teachers record a monthly snapshot of each student's skills (Listening, Speaking, Writing, Reading, Participation, Confidence, Social Skills) and behaviour (Discipline, Respect, Teamwork, Class Participation, Responsibility), plus a Teacher Remark and a Principal Remark. Each snapshot is scoped to one student, one academic year, and one calendar month, so a fresh set of ratings can be entered every month.
Select the Academic Year, Class, and Month from the filters at the top of the page.
The roster loads every student enrolled in that class for the selected month.
Rate each skill and behaviour on a 5-point scale: Needs Improvement, Fair, Good, Very Good, Excellent.
Write a Teacher Remark, or click 'AI Suggest' next to the remark box to draft one from the ratings already entered for that student. Review and edit any AI draft before saving.
Click 'Save' on a single student's row to save just that student, or 'Save Month' to save the whole class roster at once.
The page also works on a phone or tablet - the table becomes a scrollable list of cards.

content.title: Principal Remark access
content.text: Only School Admins, Principals, and Super Admins can edit the Principal Remark field. Teachers can view it, and their saves never overwrite an existing Principal Remark.

The most recently saved month's ratings and remarks for the student's academic year appear automatically on that student's Comprehensive Report (Skills Assessment, Behaviour Evaluation, and Remarks sections) - no separate step is needed to publish them to the report.
The Question Bank stores reusable questions for the paper builder and curriculum coverage.
Press 'Add Question'.
Choose Class and Subject, then the Book, Chapter and topic.
Choose the Question Type, Difficulty, Bloom's Level and Marks.
Type the Question Text. For multiple choice, enter the options and select the correct one.
Tick at least one Linked Topic. The bank lists questions by class through their topics, so a question without a topic is saved but does not appear when you filter by class.
Optionally add tags and link a Source Content Block from the book.
To find the question again, choose the Class (and Subject) in the filters at the top. The list stays empty until a class is selected.
Filter questions by keyword or semantic search, type, difficulty, Bloom level, tag and source (Human, AI Unverified, AI Verified). Mark AI-generated questions as verified after you check them.

sections.title: Question Paper Builder and Question Papers

content.title: Availability
content.text: The paper builder appears only if the feature is enabled for your school.
Paper Setup: choose Class, Subject, optional Exam, Paper Title, Total Marks, Duration and Instructions.
The Paper Title is filled in from the exam, class and subject. Edit it if you want a different title; clear it to get the suggestion back.

Paper Structure: define the sections of the paper. Sections are optional. If the section marks do not add up to the Total Marks, a 'Marks mismatch' message asks you to confirm - press Continue to go on anyway.
Choose how to add questions: 'Type manually', 'From question bank / lesson plans' or 'Capture from image' (a handwritten paper). You can change the source later.
For image capture, take a clear, well-lit photo and review the extracted questions before confirming.
Check the Curriculum Coverage and Bloom distribution panel, and fix any marks mismatch warning.
Open 'Question Papers' to see papers as Draft, Ready or Published. Resume drafts, duplicate or delete papers, and export published papers. Teachers can open Responses for a paper.

Worksheets are practice or homework sheets. Create them manually, from the question bank, or by scanning a printed sheet. Status is Draft, Ready or Published. Marks are optional because worksheets are usually ungraded. You can duplicate or delete a worksheet.
Select a Class and a Subject.
Use the Coverage Filter: All topics, Taught only, Tested only, Taught & tested, or Uncovered.
Read each topic's status, Planned Date, Taught Date, linked Lesson Plans and Questions.
Switch between 'List' and 'Timeline' views.
Summary tiles show Total Topics, Taught and Tested. This page is not shown to Manager and Staff roles.
The Finance module manages all monetary aspects of the school including fee collection, expenses, account management, discounts, and financial reporting.
Navigate to Finance > Accounts in the sidebar.
Click 'Add Account' to create finance accounts.
Account types: CASH (physical cash), BANK (bank accounts), PERSON (individual accounts).
Enter: Account Name, Type, Opening Balance.
Leave 'Visible to Staff' ticked if staff members should see this account.
Click 'Save'. The new account appears in the Manage Accounts list.
Create at least one CASH and one BANK account before collecting fees.

The Finance Dashboard is the central hub for all financial data. Use the period selector (This Month, Last Month, This Quarter, This Year, Custom) to filter data. Key metrics at a glance: Account Balance, Total Income, Total Expenses, Net Balance, and Fee Collection Rate.
Dashboard cards include: Fee Collection Summary, Account Balances, Expense Breakdown (donut chart), Recent Transfers, Monthly Trend (6-month chart), Recent Entries, and Quick Actions.

content.title: PDF Reports
content.text: Click the 'PDF' button on the dashboard header to download a comprehensive finance report with summary, account balances, monthly trends, and expense breakdown.
The Fee Setup page is a dedicated configuration page with four tabs: Monthly Structure, Annual Charges, Generate Records, and Student Discounts.
Set the monthly fee of each class, or override it for individual students.
Use the 'By Class' / 'By Student' toggle at the top to switch modes.
By Class: each class has its own card. Click 'Edit' (or '+ Set Up' for a class with no fee yet), choose the fee category and enter the amount. Use '+ Add Charge' for more categories.
By Student: select a class, then click 'Edit' to override individual student fees. Overrides are highlighted in blue. Students without an override use the class default.
Set the 'Effective From' date (when this fee amount takes effect).
Click 'Review & Save' to see a confirmation summary with the new total.
Click 'Confirm & Save'. A success message appears. Fee structures are used to auto-calculate amounts when generating fee records.

content.title: Fee Priority
content.text: Student-level fee overrides take precedence over class-level defaults. You can set a per-student override from the By Student mode.
The Annual Charges tab works the same way for yearly fees such as admission, books and fines.
Use the fee type tabs to select which type of fee to generate.
For Monthly fees: select the month and year. The system shows a preview of how many records will be created, how many already exist (will be skipped), and the total amount.
For non-monthly fees (Annual, Admission, Books, Fine): select the class to preview. The system shows per-student amounts resolved from fee structures.
Review the preview, then click 'Generate' and confirm. Fee records are created for all eligible students. Students without a fee structure or with existing records are skipped.
Fee generation requires fee structures to be set first. Students without a matching fee structure will be listed as 'no fee structure' in the preview and will not receive a record.

Assign discounts or scholarships to individual students directly from the Fee Setup page. This tab shows each student's base monthly fee, the applied discount/scholarship, and the calculated effective fee - all in one view.
Select a class from the dropdown. The student table loads with columns: Roll, Student Name, Base Fee, Discount/Scholarship, Effective Fee, and Action.
Students with an assigned discount show a colored badge (blue for discounts, purple for scholarships) and their row is highlighted green.
Click 'Assign' on a student row to open the assignment modal.
In the modal, toggle between 'Discount' and 'Scholarship', select from the dropdown (shows name, type, and value), add optional notes, then click 'Assign'.
To remove a discount, click 'Remove' on the student row and confirm.
Use the 'Bulk Assign' button to assign one discount or scholarship to all students in the selected class at once. The system shows how many were created and how many were skipped (already assigned).

content.title: Effective Fee Calculation
content.text: Percentage discounts: Effective = Base Fee - (Base Fee x Percentage / 100). Fixed discounts: Effective = Base Fee - Fixed Amount. Full scholarships: Effective = 0. The effective fee column updates instantly when a discount is assigned or removed.

content.path: Sidebar > Finance > Collect Payments > Generate Single Fee Record

content.text: Click 'Generate Single Fee Record' to open the single fee creation window.
Select a class, then search for a student using the searchable dropdown.
The fee amount auto-fills from the student's fee structure (class default or student override).
If the student has already paid, enter the paid amount. Payment fields (Account, Method, Date) appear automatically when a paid amount is entered.
The system warns if a duplicate fee record already exists for the same student/type/period.
Click 'Create' to save the fee record. A success message appears, the window closes by itself and the record shows in the fee table.

The fee collection page loads all fee records for the selected month/year in a single request. Switching class or status filters is instant (no loading delay) because filtering happens on your browser.
Four KPI cards show month-wide totals: Total Payable, Received, Balance, and Collection Rate.
Click 'Show Analytics' to reveal class-wise bar charts, payment status donut, and pending student breakdown.
Use the Fee Type, Month, Year, Class, and Status dropdowns to narrow the table view. Class and Status filters apply instantly without re-fetching data.
In the fee table, click the row's payment area or use the inline edit feature.
Enter: Amount Paid, select the receiving Account, Payment Method, and Date.
Click 'Save'. The student's status updates automatically (PAID, PARTIAL, UNPAID, ADVANCE).
Select multiple students using the checkboxes in the fee table.
The bulk action bar appears at the bottom with options to:
Set paid amount, account, and payment method for all selected records at once

Pay Full - One click to mark all selected students as fully paid (amount paid = total payable). Select an account, then click the green 'Pay Full' button. Each student's paid amount is set to their individual total (amount due + previous balance), saving time during month-end collection.
Delete all selected records (with confirmation)
Confirm the bulk action. All selected records update simultaneously.
The Discounts page has three tabs for managing discount rules, scholarship programs, and viewing all student assignments across the school.
Go to the 'Discounts' tab and click 'Add Discount'. The 'Create Discount' window opens.
Enter the Discount Name, choose the Type (Percentage or Fixed Amount) and enter the Value.
Set 'Applies To': All Students, All classes at a grade level, Specific Class, or Siblings.
Optionally set start/end dates and whether the discount is stackable.
Press 'Create Discount'. The new discount appears in the list.
Go to the 'Scholarships' tab and click 'Add Scholarship'.
Define: Name, Type (Merit, Need-Based, Sports, Staff Child, Other).
Set coverage: Full (100%), Percentage, or Fixed Amount, then press 'Create Scholarship'.

Student assignments can be managed from two places: the Discounts page (Student Assignments tab) or the Fee Setup page (Student Discounts tab). The Fee Setup page is recommended because it shows base fees and effective fees alongside the discount assignments.

content.title: Tip
content.text: Navigate to Finance > Fee Setup > Student Discounts tab for the most efficient workflow. Select a class to see all students with their base fee, assigned discount, and effective fee in one view.
Click 'Add Expense'.
Enter: Description, Category, Amount, Date, Account (which account pays).
Save. The expense is recorded and the account balance is updated.
Use category filters to view expenses by type.
Edit or delete expenses as needed.

content.title: Not enabled yet
content.text: Online fee payment is not configured for schools yet. Until it is switched on, record every payment yourself under Collect Payments (see Recording Payments).
When online payment is enabled for your school, parents can pay fees directly from their portal.
Parents will see a 'Pay Now' button on unpaid fees in their portal.
When a parent pays online, the system automatically records the payment and updates the fee balance.
Payment status is tracked: Initiated, Pending, Successful, or Failed.

content.title: Payment Security
content.text: All payment transactions use cryptographic signatures (HMAC-SHA256 for JazzCash, SHA-256 for Easypaisa) to prevent tampering. Callback URLs are verified before updating payment status.

content.title: Financial Record Safety
content.text: When a student is deleted, all their financial records (fee payments, online payments, fee structures, discounts) are preserved with 'Deleted Student' label. Best practice: mark students as inactive instead of deleting them.
Open the Transfers tab and click 'Record Transfer'.
Choose the From Account and To Account. Enter the Amount, the Date and an optional Description.
Click 'Review Transfer', check the details, then click 'Confirm Transfer'. Both account balances update and the transfer appears in the list.
At the end of each month, click 'Close Month' at the top of Finance > Accounts (admins only).
Choose the month and year. The window warns that the period will be locked.
Tick 'I understand, close this period' and click 'Close Month'.
Closing saves a Balance Brought Forward (BBF) snapshot of every account. No transactions can be added or edited in that month afterwards.
A month needs at least one transaction (payment, expense or other income) before it can be closed.
Choose Monthly or Annual view, then the month and year.
Read Category-wise Collection and the Collection Progress bar.
Use 'Generate Fee Records', 'View Summary & Collect', 'Collect Payments' or 'Fee Setup' from this page.

content.title: Tip
content.text: Fee records must be generated in Fee Setup before they appear here.
Track non-fee income such as sales and donations.
Press 'Add Income'.
Enter Date, Category, Description, Account and Amount, then save.
Filter by Month and Year. The total other income is shown at the top and each entry shows who recorded it.
To remove an entry, press Delete and confirm.

The HR module manages the complete employee lifecycle from hiring to payroll. It includes staff directory, departments, salary structures, payroll processing, leave management, attendance tracking, performance appraisals, and document management.
Click 'Add Department'. (The 'Quick Add Common Departments' chips add a department in one click.)
Enter the Department Name (e.g., 'Science', 'Administration', 'Sports') and an optional description.
Click 'Add Department' to save. A success message appears and the department is used when adding staff members.
Designations are managed in the Designations section below the departments on the same page. Click 'Add Designation', enter a name (e.g., 'Senior Teacher') and optionally link it to a department.

content.path: Sidebar > HR & Staff > Staff Directory > Full Form

content.text: Click 'Full Form'. (Use 'Quick Add' instead to enter only a name, phone, department and designation and finish the details later.)
Fill in Personal Information: First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone, Gender, Date of Birth.
Fill in Employment Details: Department, Designation, Employee ID (generated automatically if left blank), Employment Type (Full-time/Part-time/Contract), Date of Joining.
Add Address and Emergency Contact information.
Click 'Add Staff Member'. A login account is optional and can be created now or later. The staff member appears in the directory.
The Staff Directory is the central hub for managing all staff information:
Search by name, email, or employee ID
Filter by department or employment status (Active, On Leave, Terminated)
Click on a staff member to view/edit their complete profile
Export directory as Excel or PDF
Click 'Add Salary Structure' and choose the staff member.
Enter the Basic Salary, then add any Allowances (e.g., house rent) and Deductions (e.g., tax) as name and amount pairs with '+ Add'. The summary shows the net salary.
Set 'Effective From' (and optionally 'Effective To'), then click 'Create'.
Salary structures feed directly into payroll generation. A staff member needs one before a payslip can be generated.
Select the month and year for payroll.
Click 'Generate Payslips', then 'Generate' to confirm. Payslips are created for active staff who have a salary structure; existing payslips for the month are skipped.
Review generated payslips. Check amounts, deductions, and net pay.
Approve payslips individually or in bulk.
Mark approved payslips as 'Paid' once payment is disbursed.

Click the 'Download PDF' button on any payslip (or the 'PDF' button on its row) to download a printable payslip document, saved as payslip_<Name>_<month>_<year>.pdf. The PDF includes the school logo (if configured in school settings), school name, address, contact details, employee information, earnings breakdown, deductions breakdown, net salary, and signature lines.

content.title: School Logo on Payslips
content.text: The payslip PDF automatically includes your school's logo at the top if one is configured. To set or update the logo, go to Settings > School Profile and enter the logo URL. If no logo is set, the payslip generates without it.
The leave system handles leave applications, approvals, and balance tracking:
Staff submit leave requests specifying: Leave Type, From Date, To Date, Reason.
A School Admin or Principal reviews the request.
Approve or reject the leave application with optional remarks.
Leave balances update automatically upon approval.
View leave history and balances for any staff member.
Select the date to mark attendance.
Mark each staff member as Present, Absent, or On Leave.
Save. Staff attendance records feed into payroll calculations.
Click 'Create Appraisal' and select the staff member.
Fill in performance criteria, ratings, and comments.
Submit the appraisal for review.
Appraisal history is maintained per staff member.
Select a staff member.
Upload documents: ID proofs, certificates, contracts, etc.
Documents are stored securely and accessible from the staff profile.

Staff members can be linked to existing user accounts so the same person's HR record and login credentials are connected. This is useful when a user account was created separately from the staff record.
Find the staff member in the directory. If they have no linked account, you will see a 'Link Account' button.
Click 'Link Account' to open the search modal.
Search for the user by name or username. Click on the correct user to link them.
Once linked, the staff member's account column shows the linked username and role.
To unlink, click the 'Unlink' button next to the linked username. This removes the association but does not delete either the staff record or the user account.
A user can only be linked to one staff member at a time. If the user is already linked to another staff record, you must unlink them first.

The Letter Composer allows you to create official letters on your school's letterhead. It supports 7 built-in templates (Experience Certificate, Termination, Warning, Appreciation, Leave Approval, Salary Increment, Transfer) and fully custom letters.
Select a Quick Draft Template to start with a pre-built letter structure, or choose 'Custom Letter'.
Pick a recipient: select from School, Employee, or type a custom address. Selecting an employee auto-fills placeholders like name, department, and designation.
Edit the Subject and Body. Use the formatting toolbar: *bold*, _italic_, ~strikethrough~, bullet lists, and numbered lists.
Preview your letter in the right panel (live preview updates as you type).
Click 'Generate PDF' to download the letter as a PDF with your school's letterhead as background.
Letters are automatically saved to history. Load, edit, or delete past letters from the history table.

content.title: AI Letter Drafting
content.text: Click 'Draft with AI' to open the AI assistant panel. Describe the letter you need in plain language (e.g., 'Write a warning letter for late attendance') and the AI will generate a complete subject and body. Quick suggestion chips are provided for common letter types. If an employee is selected, their details are automatically included for context. Review and edit the AI-generated content before generating the PDF.

content.title: School Letterhead
content.text: Letters are generated with your school's letterhead as the PDF background. To configure the letterhead, go to Settings > School Profile and set the Letterhead URL (uploaded to Supabase Storage). If no letterhead is set, letters generate on a white background.

Staff accounts have a Self Service page with two tabs: Leave (your own leave requests) and Attendance (your own staff attendance). Teachers see the same pages as 'My Leave' and 'My Attendance' in the sidebar.
The Admissions CRM manages the complete student enrollment pipeline from initial enquiry to final enrollment. It tracks leads, followups, and conversion rates.

Admissions uses the school's academic years (set up in Management > Sessions). When converting enquiries to students, you select the target academic year and class. The system creates the student record and enrolls them in that session.
Click 'New Enquiry'.
Fill in: Student Name, Father Name, Mobile and Grade Applied For.
Set Source: Walk-in, Phone Call, Website, WhatsApp, Referral, Social Media, Ad Campaign or Other.
Optionally set the Next Follow-up Date and add notes.
Click 'Create Enquiry'. The enquiry appears in the list with status New.
Each enquiry progresses through these stages:

rows: Admission confirmed - ready for conversion to student
Converted to a student record with enrollment

content.text: View all enquiries in a searchable table or card view. Search by child name or phone number.
Filter by Grade and Source. Click a stage in the Admission funnel to filter by status.
The Admission funnel at the top shows the count for each stage (New, Confirmed, Converted, Cancelled) and the conversion rate.
Use 'Edit' to update enquiry details, 'Cancel' to mark an enquiry as cancelled, or 'Delete' to remove one that is not yet converted.
Click 'Confirm' on a New enquiry when the admission is approved.
Click 'Edit' on the enquiry.
Set the Next Follow-up Date and write what was discussed in Notes, then click 'Update Enquiry'.
The date shows in the Follow-up column of the Enquiries list, in red once it is overdue.
Confirmed enquiries can be batch-converted into student records. Each converted student gets a Student record and a StudentEnrollment record linking them to the chosen academic year.
Select one or more enquiries with 'Confirmed' status using the checkboxes.
Click the 'Convert to students' button in the bar that appears.
In the modal, select the target Academic Year and Class & Section. Optionally tick 'Auto-generate fee records' and choose the fee types.
Click 'Convert N Enquiries'. Roll numbers are auto-assigned sequentially within that session and class.
Converted enquiries change status to 'Converted' and link to the created student.

content.title: Session-Scoped Admissions
content.text: You can admit students into any academic year, including a future session. Roll numbers start from 1 for each session-class combination, independent of other sessions. This means admissions work even before running promotion for the current year.

content.title: Admissions and Promotion Relationship
content.text: Admissions create enrollment in the selected academic year directly. Promotion manages existing enrolled students between years. If you admit future-year students before promotion, that is valid and expected because roll numbers are scoped per academic year and class/session class.
The enquiries page provides at-a-glance analytics:
Admission funnel - Count of enquiries in each stage (New, Confirmed, Converted, Cancelled)
Conversion Rate - Percentage of enquiries that become students
Source Tracking - Which channels (Walk-in, Referral, etc.) bring the most enquiries
The Transport module manages school buses, routes, student-bus assignments, and daily transport attendance.
Click 'Add Route'.

Enter: Route Name, Start Location, End Location and Estimated Duration (minutes) - these four are required. Description and Distance (km) are optional. You can also click the maps to mark the start and end points.
Click 'Create Route'. The route appears in the list.
Click 'Stops' on the route, then '+ Add Stop'.
For each stop, enter: Stop Name, Order, Pickup Time and Drop Time (all required). Address and a map location are optional.
Click 'Add Stop'. Stops are listed in order. Use Edit or Delete on a stop to change it, and Duplicate on a route to copy it with all its stops.
Click 'Add Vehicle'.
Enter: Vehicle Number, Vehicle Type (Bus, Van or Car) and Capacity. Make / Model is optional.
Under Driver Information enter the Driver Name and Driver Phone (required). The Driver License Number is optional.
Choose the Assigned Route this vehicle serves (optional).
Click 'Add Vehicle'. The vehicle appears in the list, linked to the route.
Click 'New Assignment'.
Search for a student by name or roll number and click the name. Repeat to add several students at once; they appear as chips above the list.
Choose the Route, then the Stop (both required). Choosing a Vehicle is optional; only vehicles on that route are listed. Set the Transport Type: Pickup Only, Drop Only or Both.
Click 'Assign'. A student can have one assignment per academic year; students who already have one are skipped.
Use the filters to find assignments by route, class or type, and 'Remove' to delete one.
Select the date (today by default) and the route. The students assigned to it are listed.
Everyone starts as Boarded. Click 'Not Boarded' or 'Absent' for the students who did not ride.
Click 'Save All'. One record is saved per student, per route, per day; saving again for the same day updates it.
The Transport Dashboard shows:
Total Routes - Number of active routes
Total Vehicles - Number of active vehicles
Students Assigned - Students with an active transport assignment
Today's Attendance - Students whose transport attendance was recorded today
Only School Admins and Principals can add or change Transport data; other roles can view it.

The Library module provides a complete book management system including cataloging, issuing/returning books, and tracking overdue items. Only School Admins and Principals can change anything here; other staff roles can browse the catalog and see which books are out.
On the Book Catalog page, click 'Manage Categories'.
Type a Category Name (for example Fiction, Science, Mathematics, History, Reference), add an optional description and click 'Add Category'.
Use Edit to rename a category, or Delete to remove it. Its books stay in the catalog without a category.
Category names must be unique. Categories help organize and filter the book catalog.
Click 'Add Book'.
Enter Title and Author (both required), then ISBN, Publisher, Category, Total Copies and Shelf Location.
Click 'Add Book'. The book appears in the catalog with all copies available.
Use the search bar to find books by title, author, or ISBN, and the Category filter to browse one section.
Edit changes a book. Total Copies cannot go below the copies currently issued.
A book that has ever been issued cannot be deleted because its history is kept. Edit it and untick Active to take it off the shelf instead.
On the 'Issue Book' tab, choose Student or Staff as the Borrower Type.
Type at least two letters of the borrower's name and pick them from the list.
Type at least two letters of the book title and pick the book (only books with copies available are listed).
Check the Due Date. It starts at today plus the loan period set in Library Settings (14 days by default).
Add optional notes and click 'Issue Book'. The book's available copies drop by 1.

A borrower cannot go over the limit set in Library Settings (3 books for a student, 5 for staff by default) or take a second copy of the same book. You can also start from the catalog: click 'Issue' next to a book.
Open the 'Return Book' tab and search by student name, staff name or book title.
Click 'Process Return' next to the entry.
Check the summary. For a late book it shows the days overdue and the fine (days overdue x the daily fine in Library Settings).
Click 'Confirm Return'. The book's available copies increase by 1 and the fine is recorded on the issue.
The page lists every book past its due date that has not come back, oldest first, with the borrower, days overdue and the fine so far.
The summary shows the number of overdue books, the total estimated fines and the fine per day.
Click 'Return' on a row to take the book back and record its fine.
Due-date reminders to borrowers and parents are sent by the Notifications module's on-demand job, not from this page.
The Library Dashboard displays:
Book Titles - Number of active titles in the catalog
Total Copies - Sum of all copies of active titles
Currently Issued - Books checked out and not yet returned
Overdue Books - Issued books past their due date
Categories - Number of book categories
Most Issued Books - The five most borrowed titles
School Admins and Principals also get a 'Library Settings' button for the loan period, the borrowing limits for students and staff, and the fine per overdue day.

The LMS module provides curriculum management (books, chapters, topics), lesson planning, assignments, and student submissions. It integrates with the Academics module and supports multiple languages including Urdu, Arabic, Sindhi, Pashto, and Punjabi with RTL text display.
The Curriculum page lets you organize textbooks into a Book > Chapter > Topic hierarchy for each class and subject. This structure powers syllabus progress tracking and lesson plan topic selection.
Select a Class and Subject from the filter dropdowns.
Click 'Add Book'. Choose the Class and Subject, enter the Title, and optionally the Author, Publisher, Edition, Language and Description, then click 'Add Book'. The toast 'Book created' confirms it.
Click the book to view its chapters and topics in the tree view.
Click 'Add Chapter' (Title, Chapter Number, Description) and, inside a chapter, 'Add Topic' (Title, Topic Number, Estimated Periods, Description). Or use 'Import Table of Contents' for bulk import.
The Import Table of Contents window has two tabs:
Manual Entry: type or paste the table of contents text with indentation for chapter/topic structure, then click 'Next: Review'.
Upload Photo: upload a photo of the book's printed contents page. The system extracts the text with OCR so you can review it.
Review and edit the chapters and topics, then apply them to create the structure.

content.title: Multi-Language Support
content.text: The OCR feature supports all configured languages. For non-English books, the system uses the book's language setting to optimize text recognition. The editor displays RTL direction automatically for supported languages.
A progress bar shows how many topics have been covered by published lesson plans. Topics are automatically marked as covered when a teacher publishes a lesson plan referencing them.
This page is not available to the Manager role.
Click 'Add Lesson Plan'. This opens the bulk wizard; click 'Create single lesson plan' for one plan.
Choose Minimal (Class, Subject, chapters/topics, Lesson Date, Teacher; saved as a Draft with an automatic title) or Standard (full details).
In Standard mode enter Title, Description and Objectives, then set Duration (minutes), Materials Needed and Teaching Methods.
Standard mode also has a Status of Draft or Published. Click 'Create Lesson Plan'; the toast 'Lesson plan created successfully!' confirms it.
A Draft can be published later with the 'Publish' button on its row.
Click 'Create Assignment'.
Enter the Title, then select Class, Subject and Teacher.
Choose the Assignment Type: Homework, Project, Classwork or Lab. Diary entries use 'Create Daily Diary' instead.
Set the Due Date (required when 'Require student submission' is on) and Total Marks; turn 'Allow file attachments' on or off.
Enter the Description (required) and Instructions.
Click 'Create Assignment'. New assignments start as Draft; click 'Publish' on the row to make them appear in student portals.
Click the number in the Submissions column of an assignment (or the 'Submissions' button in card view).
For each submission you can view the submitted text or attached file, enter Marks and Feedback, and click 'Grade' then 'Save'.
Graded submissions can be re-graded or sent back to the student with 'Return'.
The cards at the top count Total, Submitted, Graded, Returned, Pending and Late submissions.
The Notifications module enables school-wide communication with students, parents, and staff. Admins can create templates, send bulk notifications, and track delivery.
Click the Notification Bell icon in the top bar for a quick dropdown (shows 8 most recent). The bell bounces when new notifications arrive.
Or navigate to 'Notifications' in the sidebar for the full Inbox tab with pagination.

Unread notifications stand out with a bold white card; click a notification to mark it as read (it also opens the related page, such as Fee Collection). Older ones are grouped under Today, Yesterday and Earlier.
Use 'Mark all read' (with confirmation) to clear all unread notifications at once.
Filter with the 'All Types' dropdown (Absence, Fee Due, Exam Result, Transport Update, etc.) or tick 'Unread only'.
Switch to the 'Templates' tab.
Click 'New Template'.
Enter a Template Name, pick the Event Type and Channel, add an optional Subject, and write the Message body (placeholders use double braces, like {{student_name}}).
Click 'Save'. Use Edit, Duplicate, Preview or Delete on any row later; untick 'Active' to hide a template from the Send tab. Templates marked 'Shared' belong to every school and cannot be changed.
Switch to the 'Send' tab.
Choose the mode: 'Broadcast to Group' for everyone in a role, or 'Single Recipient' for one person (phone, email or user ID).
In Broadcast mode, select a group: All Parents, All Teachers, All Staff, All Admins, Principals, Managers, Accountants, or All Students. Optionally narrow parents or students to one session class.
Optionally pick an existing template to pre-fill the message, or compose a custom message.
Choose the channel: In-App (also delivered as a mobile push notification) or Email.

Click 'Review & Send Broadcast', check the estimated recipients, then 'Confirm Send' (Single mode: 'Send Notification'). If the text still contains {{placeholders}} a warning appears first; manual sends do not fill them in. A message shows how many were sent, skipped or failed. 'Test Send to Me' sends a copy to your own inbox.

content.title: Run Now buttons
content.text: At the top of the Send tab, 'Send Fee Reminders Now', 'Generate Daily Report Now' and 'Remind Teachers to Mark Attendance' fire this school's automatic notifications on demand.
Track notification effectiveness with configurable date ranges (7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or all time):
Delivery Rate - How many notifications were successfully delivered
Read Rate - Percentage of notifications opened/read
Breakdown by channel (In-App, Email, Push) and event type

Configure notification channels, smart scheduling (AI-optimized send times), and automated notification controls from the Settings tab. Each automation type can be toggled ON/OFF per school. Toggles are module-aware: if a module (e.g., Transport, Finance) is disabled for the school, its related toggles are automatically hidden.

rows: Bus departed, arriving at stop, journey completed
AI learns optimal send times over 2-4 weeks

content.text: The Settings tab also warns you about unsaved changes before navigating away. Channel toggles cover In-App and Email; push notifications are delivered together with In-App.

content.title: Background Tasks
content.text: Scheduled notifications such as absence summaries, fee reminders and attendance reminders run automatically. No manual action required.

The Messaging module provides a unified, threaded conversation system for all school roles. Admins, Teachers, Staff, Parents, and Students can exchange messages with role-based access controls determining who can contact whom.

rows: Any staff member in the school
Parents of students in their classes
Students with accounts in their classes

content.text: All roles access the same Messages page from the sidebar. The page shows a split-panel layout: thread list on the left, conversation view on the right. On mobile devices, the view switches between list and conversation.
Click the 'New Message' button (top of the thread list).
Pick who to write to using the Staff, Parent or Student tabs, then search for the name in the 'To' box.
For teacher-parent/student conversations, the student context is automatically set based on the recipient.
Optionally enter a subject line for the conversation.
Type your message and click 'Send Message'.

content.title: Thread Reuse
content.text: If you already have an active conversation with the same person (and same student context), your new message will be added to the existing thread instead of creating a duplicate.
Click on any thread in the thread list to open the conversation.
All messages in the thread are displayed chronologically (oldest first).
Your messages appear on the right side, the other person's on the left.
Type your reply in the box at the bottom, then press Enter or click the paper-plane button (Shift+Enter starts a new line).
The thread is automatically marked as read when you open it.

Unread threads are highlighted in the thread list with a blue badge showing the unread message count. The Messages navigation item in the sidebar also shows a total unread count badge. The badge updates automatically every 15 seconds.
Use the search box at the top of the thread list to filter conversations.
Search matches against participant names and the latest message preview.
Parents have a dedicated portal to monitor their children's school activities. Parents can view attendance, fees, timetable, exam results, and communicate with the school.
After logging in, parents see their dashboard with:
List of linked children (if multiple children attend the school)
Quick action cards for common tasks (Apply Leave, Messages)
Recent notifications from the school
On the dashboard, click 'Overview' on a child's card to open their overview page.
The header shows the child's photo, name, class and roll number.
Four cards summarise: Attendance Rate, Fees (amount due, or 'Nothing due'), Last Exam and Days Present.
Under 'Details', choose Attendance Calendar, Fee Details, Timetable, Exam Schedule or Exam Results for the full pages.
Click 'Attendance' to view the child's attendance records.
See monthly and daily breakdowns with Present/Absent/Late counts.
View attendance percentage and trends.
View fee balance, payment history, and outstanding amounts.
See due amounts and upcoming fee deadlines.
Download fee receipts for past payments.

content.title: Not enabled yet
content.text: Online payment is not available yet. Pay at the school office until your school announces it.

content.path: Parent Portal > Child > Fees > Pay Now

content.text: If the school has configured online payment gateways, a 'Pay Now' button appears next to each unpaid fee.
Click 'Pay Now' on the fee you wish to pay.
A modal appears showing available payment methods (e.g., JazzCash, Easypaisa, Manual Transfer).
Select your preferred payment method and click 'Proceed to Pay'.
For JazzCash/Easypaisa: You will be redirected to the gateway's checkout page to complete payment.
For Manual Transfer: Bank account details are displayed. Make the transfer and inform the school office.
After payment, you are redirected to a Payment Result page showing the transaction status.
Payment statuses: Successful (green), Pending (yellow - being verified), Failed (red - try again).
Pending payments are automatically verified within a few minutes. The page auto-refreshes.

content.title: Online Payment Availability
content.text: Online payments are only available if your school's administration has switched online payment on. If you don't see the Pay Now button, pay at the school office.
View the child's class timetable.
See subjects, teachers, and period timings for each day.
View exam marks and grades (once published by the school).
See subject-wise marks, percentage and grade for each exam.
Click 'Leave Requests' in the sidebar. The 'Apply for Leave' tab opens first.
Select the child, then enter Start Date, End Date and Reason. A supporting document link is optional.
Click 'Submit Leave Request'. The message 'Leave request submitted successfully.' appears.
Open the 'My Requests' tab to track the status (Pending, Approved, Rejected or Cancelled) and read the school's remarks.
A request that is still Pending can be cancelled with 'Cancel'.
Parents can send and receive threaded messages with their children's teachers. See the Messaging chapter for full details on how conversations work.
Students have their own portal to view attendance, timetable, assignments, fees, exam results, and manage their profile.
The Student Dashboard displays:
Welcome card with student name and class
Attendance rate (percentage)
Assignment stats (pending, submitted, graded)
Fee balance summary
Today's timetable
Upcoming assignment deadlines
View your attendance history with monthly/daily breakdown.
See attendance percentage and trend over time.
View your class timetable for each day of the week.
See subject names, teacher names, and period timings.
The page lists every assignment from your teachers with its subject, type, due date and status.
Diary entries are for reading only; they have no Submit button.
Click 'Submit' on an open assignment, type your answer in Submission Text (required), and optionally add a link to your file and a file name.
Click 'Submit Assignment'. The message 'Assignment submitted successfully!' appears. Late work is marked Late.
After the teacher grades it, the card shows your marks and feedback. Closed assignments can no longer be submitted.
View your fee balance and payment history.
See upcoming due dates.
Each published exam appears as a card with your total, percentage and grade. Click its title to open or close the subject table.
The table lists marks, total marks, percentage and a Pass or Fail badge for each subject; an absent paper shows 'Absent'.
View and update your profile information.
See contact details and class information.

The AI Study Helper is an intelligent chatbot that assists students with their studies. It is aware of the student's class, subjects, lesson plans, and assignments, allowing it to provide personalized, curriculum-aligned academic support.
Navigate to 'AI Study Helper' in the student sidebar.
Type your study question in the message box at the bottom of the screen.
Click Send or press Enter to submit your question.
The AI will respond with explanations, examples, and study tips tailored to your curriculum.
Your conversation history is saved and can be reviewed later.
Use the suggestion chips (e.g., 'Help me understand fractions', 'Explain photosynthesis') for quick prompts.
Click 'Clear Chat' to start a fresh conversation.

content.title: Daily Limit
content.text: Students can send up to 30 messages per day to the AI Study Helper. The counter resets every 24 hours. This ensures fair usage for all students.
The AI Study Helper is designed for academic topics only. Questions about personal information, violence, or other inappropriate content will be blocked by the safety system.

The Hostel Management module helps schools manage their boarding facilities. It covers hostel buildings, rooms, student allocations, and gate passes for students leaving and returning to the hostel. Hostel pages are available to School Admin and Principal roles only, because they list students and the reasons for their leave.
The Hostel Dashboard provides a quick overview of all hostel operations:
Total hostels and rooms, total capacity and current occupancy
Occupancy rate (percentage of available beds filled) and available beds
Pending gate pass requests
Students currently out on gate passes
Number of boys' and girls' hostels
Quick action links to manage rooms, allocations, and gate passes
Navigate to Hostel > Rooms in the sidebar. The 'Hostels' tab is open.
Click 'Add Hostel'.
Enter the Hostel Name, choose the Hostel Type (Boys / Girls / Mixed) and enter the Capacity.
Optionally enter the Address and Contact Number, and choose a Warden from your active staff.
Click 'Add Hostel'. The hostel appears in the list with its occupancy.
Open the 'Rooms' tab and choose a hostel in 'Select Hostel'.
Click 'Add Room'.
Enter the Room Number, Floor and Capacity, and choose the Room Type (Single / Double / Dormitory).
Click 'Add Room'. The room shows its occupancy and whether it is Available, Full or Unavailable.

content.title: Room status
content.text: A room shows Full when every bed is taken. Untick 'Available for allocation' when you take a room out of use; it is then shown as Unavailable and cannot be chosen for new allocations. A room's capacity cannot be lowered below the number of students in it.
A hostel or room that has student allocation records cannot be deleted, so the history is kept. Mark a hostel Inactive, or a room Unavailable, instead.
Allocations assign students to specific hostel rooms for an academic year. The list can be filtered by hostel, by status (Active or Vacated) and searched by student name.
Navigate to Hostel > Allocations and click 'Allocate Student'.
The Academic Year is the current one. Search for and choose the Student; students who already hold a bed this year are not listed.
Choose the Hostel, then a Room. Only rooms with a free bed are listed.
Click 'Allocate'. The student appears in the list with the room.
Find the active allocation in the list and click 'Vacate'.
Confirm. The allocation is marked Vacated with today's date and the room's occupancy decreases.
Choose 'Vacated' in the status filter to see students who have left.

Each student can only hold one active hostel bed per academic year. Vacate the current allocation before placing the student in another room; a vacated student can be allocated again in the same year.
Gate passes track students leaving and returning to the hostel. They follow a workflow: Request > Approve/Reject > Check Out > Return.
Click 'New Gate Pass'.
Choose the Student (only students who currently hold a hostel bed are listed) and the Pass Type (Day Pass / Overnight / Weekend / Vacation Leave).
Enter the Reason and where the student is Going To, and optionally a contact number at the destination.
The Departure Date and Expected Return are filled in (the next full hour, and eight hours later); change them if needed, then click 'Create Gate Pass'. The pass starts as Pending Approval.
Review pending gate passes in the list.
Click 'Approve' to authorize the student's departure, or 'Reject' to deny the request.
Add optional remarks in the box and confirm.
When the student leaves the gate, click 'Check Out' on the approved pass.
When the student is back, click 'Mark Returned'. The actual return time is recorded.

rows: Mark Returned when student comes back

content.text: The Settings page has two tabs: Profile (your own account and school preferences such as Examination Settings) and Users (School Admins and Principals manage user accounts there).

content.path: Sidebar > Settings > School Profile > Examination Settings

content.text: Toggle between Simple Average and Weighted Average for report card calculations. When Weighted Average is enabled, each exam type's contribution is scaled by its weight (configured in Exam Types). See Chapter 6 (Examinations) for details.
See Chapter 7 (Finance Module) > Setting Up Finance Accounts for detailed instructions.

content.title: Not enabled yet
content.text: Online payment gateways are not configured for schools yet, so there is nothing to set up here. Record fee payments under Finance > Collect Payments. This section will be updated when online payments are switched on.
Education AI uses a hierarchical role system for user management. School Admins and Principals can create and manage users within their schools.
The system has the following roles, listed from highest to lowest privilege:

rows: Principal, Manager, Accountant, Teacher, Staff, Driver
Own classes: Attendance, Academics, Content Creation, Planning
Parent portal: own child's data only

content.title: What you see
content.text: The sidebar also depends on which modules your school has enabled. If you cannot see a page, your role or your school's modules do not include it.
School Admins and Principals can create, edit, and deactivate user accounts for their school from the Users tab in Settings.
Navigate to Settings and click the 'Users' tab.
Click 'Add User' to open the user creation form.
Fill in First name, Last name, Username (required), Email, Password, Confirm password, select a Role from the dropdown, and add a Phone number if you want.
The role dropdown only shows roles you are allowed to create based on your role.
Click 'Create User' to save. A school membership is automatically created.
To edit a user, click 'Edit' in the actions column. You can change name, email, role, and phone.

To reset a forgotten password, click 'Reset Password' on the user's row. Choose 'Set a new password now' and type the New Password (at least 8 characters) twice, or choose 'Email a reset link' (only available when the user has an email address), then press 'Reset Password' or 'Send Email'.
To deactivate a user, click 'Deactivate'. The user will no longer be able to log in.
To reactivate, click 'Activate' on an inactive user.

content.title: Role Restrictions
content.text: You can only edit or deactivate users whose role you are allowed to create. For example, a Principal cannot deactivate a School Admin.
When adding a new student, you can optionally create a user account so the student can access the Student Portal.
Open the Add Student modal and fill in the student details (Class, Name, Roll Number).
Check the 'Create User Account (Student Portal)' checkbox at the bottom of the form.
Additional fields will appear: Username (auto-suggested from student name), Email, Password, and Confirm Password.
Fill in the login credentials. Password must be at least 8 characters.
Click 'Add Student'. Both the student record and user account will be created together.
The student can now log in to the Student Portal using these credentials.

Students without accounts show 'No Account' in the Account column. Individual: Click 'Create Account' next to any student, fill in credentials, and save. Bulk: Select multiple students using checkboxes, click 'Create Accounts' in the floating bar, set a default password, and confirm. Usernames are auto-generated (e.g., 'Ahmed Khan' becomes 'ahmed_khan').

When adding a new staff member (full form or Quick Add), check 'Create User Account' to set up login credentials alongside the staff record. Select a User Role (Teacher, Staff, Manager, Accountant, Driver) to determine system access level.

Staff without accounts show 'No Account' in the Account column. Individual: Click 'Create Account', set role and credentials. Bulk: Select multiple staff, click 'Create Accounts', choose default role and password. Usernames are auto-generated (e.g., 'Jane Doe' becomes 'jane_doe').

sections.title: Linking Existing User Accounts to Staff

content.text: If a user account already exists separately (e.g., created before the staff record), you can link them from the Staff Directory. Click 'Link Account' on the staff row, search for the user, and select them. To unlink, click the 'Unlink' button. See Chapter 8 (HR & Staff > Linking & Unlinking User Accounts) for full details.
Passwords cannot be recovered. If a user forgets their password, a School Admin must reset it from the Users tab.
Education AI includes AI-assisted features that help with everyday work: dashboard insights, timetable generation, report card comments and letter drafting. Always review AI output before sharing it.

The admin dashboard surfaces AI-generated actionable insights across all modules: Alerts (red) for urgent issues, Warnings (amber) for important items, and Info (blue) for setup reminders. Each insight links directly to the relevant page. Insights are role-specific (teachers see attendance only, accountants see finance only).

Timetable auto-generation supports two algorithms: 'Quick (Greedy)' for near-instant drafts, and 'Optimal (OR-Tools)' for higher quality schedules (up to 30 seconds). OR-Tools enforces hard constraints (no double-booking) and optimizes subject distribution across days.

Generate personalized comments for each student's exam performance based on marks, grades, and attendance. Click 'Generate AI Comments' on an exam's results page. Comments appear on report cards automatically. Teachers should review before sharing with parents.

content.title: Fallback
content.text: Without a Groq API key, the system generates rule-based comments automatically.

content.path: Sidebar > HR & Staff > Letter Composer > Draft with AI

content.text: The Letter Composer includes an AI assistant that drafts professional letters from natural language descriptions. Enter a prompt like 'Write a warning letter for late attendance' or 'Draft an experience certificate for Rajesh who joined 3 years ago as a Math teacher' and the AI generates a complete subject and body. The AI uses template context (if a template type is selected) and employee details (if an employee is selected) for more accurate drafts. Quick suggestion chips are provided for common letter types.

content.title: Fallback
content.text: Without a Groq API key, the system matches keywords in your prompt to built-in templates and returns the closest matching template. You can always edit the content manually.

Students flagged by the attendance risk predictor, showing current attendance, predicted attendance in 4 weeks and a trend (Declining, Stable, Improving). Filter by severity (High, Medium, Low) and class. School Admin and Principal only.
A combined risk score that blends attendance, fee default likelihood and academic performance. Filter by severity and class. School Admin and Principal only.
Students trending toward failing grades, showing their average and predicted next exam with a trend. Filter by severity and class. School Admin and Principal only.
Staff flagged for rising leave frequency or declining attendance, showing leave days (last 90 days), absence rate and trend. Filter by severity and department. School Admin and Principal only.
Risk scores are AI estimates meant to start a conversation, not a final judgment about a person. Select an academic year first for the student pages.
The Inventory module tracks store items, stock movements and items assigned to staff. It is available to School Admins and Principals.
Shows Total Items, Total Stock Value, Active Assignments, Low Stock Alerts and Recent Transactions, with quick links to the other pages.
Click the 'Categories' and 'Vendors' buttons at the top first and add the categories and vendors you use.
Add an item: Name, Category, Unit (Pieces, Packets, Boxes, Kilograms, Litres, Sets, Reams, Dozens, Metres), Current Stock, Minimum Stock, Unit Price and Storage Location.
Filter the list by category and stock status: In Stock, Low Stock or Out of Stock.
Use 'AI Suggest' to get suggested items for the kind of school you describe, select the ones you want and add them.

School Admins and Principals record stock movements here; other roles with inventory access can only view the history. Issues and Returns are not entered by hand: they are created automatically when you assign an item or mark it returned (see Item Assignments).
Press '+ Record Transaction'.
Choose the type: Purchase (new stock from a vendor), Adjustment (correct a stock count) or Disposal (damaged or expired items).
Select the Item. Its current stock is shown in the list and its unit price is filled in for you.
Enter the Quantity. For a Disposal enter a positive number; the stock is reduced for you. For an Adjustment use a negative number to reduce stock. Stock can never go below zero.

Choose the Vendor (Purchase only), set the Date, add a Reference number such as an invoice or PO, and any Remarks, then press 'Record Transaction'. A 'Transaction recorded' message appears and the item's stock updates.
Filter the history by Type and by From and To dates. Issue and Return rows created by assignments appear here too.
School Admins and Principals assign items and mark them returned. Accountants, Teachers and Staff can only view assignments (Teachers and Staff see just the items assigned to them).
Press '+ Assign Item'.

Choose the Item (only items in stock are listed) and the person under 'Assign To' (active staff accounts), set the Quantity, pick the item's Condition (New, Good, Fair or Poor) and add notes such as a serial number, then press 'Assign'. The assignment is dated today, the stock is reduced and an Issue transaction is recorded.
Switch between the 'Active' and 'Returned' tabs, and search by person or item name.
When the item comes back, press 'Return' on its row, choose its condition and press 'Confirm Return'. The stock is restored and a Return transaction is recorded.
Items flagged by the AI as low on stock or projected to run out, with severity (High, Medium, Low), current stock, projected stockout time and trend.
Class dropdowns are session-scoped: always select the correct academic year first to see the right class list
Use bulk import (Excel) for students when starting with a large number of records
Use search and filter features to quickly find records in any list
Export data regularly as backups (Excel, PDF)
Use strong, unique passwords; log out when leaving the computer unattended
Regularly review user access and deactivate unused accounts
The User Guide covers pages for all roles; if you cannot see a page, your role or school modules do not include it
Manual: Press Mark All Present, then change only the exceptions; save before leaving the page
Face: Enroll all students first; use clear portraits (quality > 70%); good lighting for group photos
Face: Avoid backlighting; review yellow-flagged matches; re-enroll after major appearance changes
If attendance was already marked, reopen the same class and date: saving updates the records and never duplicates them
Attendance cannot be saved on OFF days
Set up accounts before the academic year; close months regularly
Use discounts/scholarships feature instead of manual fee adjustments
Use 'Pay Full' bulk action for quick month-end collection
Download PDF reports monthly from the Finance Dashboard for record-keeping
